title: Your Life as an NBA Player at Every Level (60% Go Broke)
hook: The odds of ever getting here are 0.03%. The odds of staying rich once you do are worse.
body: POV: a composite hopeful who beats odds almost nobody clears -- from a driveway hoop bolted above a garage (VERIFIED: roughly 0.03% of U.S. high school players ever reach the NBA) through a Division I roster (VERIFIED: about 1% of NCAA players are ever drafted) to undrafted G League grinding (VERIFIED: $40,500/season) and a two-way contract (VERIFIED: $578,577, exactly half the 2025-26 rookie minimum) to a drafted rookie (VERIFIED: $1,361,969 rookie minimum) to a career-threatening ACL tear (VERIFIED: the average NBA career lasts just 4.5 years) to a real 10-day-contract comeback, an All-Star nod, and a supermax superstar contract (VERIFIED: grounded in the real 2025 record, a 5-year, $313,933,410 deal) -- to the reckoning every level eventually meets. The coda fact nobody puts on a banner: an estimated 60% of former NBA players are broke within five years of retirement (Sports Illustrated's landmark investigation, reconfirmed by later reporting). You, Denise, Coach Ellis, Marcus, and Priya Osei are a FICTIONAL COMPOSITE; no real, named NBA player is depicted as this episode's protagonist. Watch the whole series -- every life, every level, every ladder somebody has to climb from the bottom. For educational and entertainment purposes.
pinned: Real fact: an estimated 60% of former NBA players are broke within five years of retirement (Sports Illustrated investigation). The average NBA career lasts just 4.5 years. The 2025-26 rookie minimum is $1,361,969; the largest supermax on record is over $313 million. Which level would you stop climbing at?
poll: Which level costs the most? LEVEL 01 (The Driveway -- 0.03% odds of ever getting here) / LEVEL 04 (The Call-Up -- an ACL tear, 2 seasons in) / LEVEL 07 (Supermax -- $313.9M, four visits home a year) / LEVEL 08 (The Reckoning -- retired, and 60% go broke)
